en: The Mahāśīta-vana-ārya-dhanada-dhāraṇī-sūtra.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Great Dharma Teacher, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject [Amoghavajra], at Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India, in the Kingdom of the Western Heavens.
Translated by Fǎtiàn by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavān was staying in the city of Rājagṛha.
At that time, the Venerable Rāhula was wandering in the Śītavana cemetery within the region of Uruvilvā.
He was among the great charnel grounds.
At that time, there were various celestial spirits, nāga spirits, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kinnaras, mahoragas, garuḍas,
and all other humans and non-humans.
They are possessed by pretas, bhūtas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and the like; furthermore,
there are many kinds of diverse creatures such as crows,
magpies, wild foxes, jackals, wolves, insects, and ants.
Being extremely troubled and distressed,
the Venerable Rāhula then went to where the Buddha was staying. Upon arrival,
he prostrated himself with his head to the ground.
He prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, circumambulated him three times,
and stood before the World-Honored One weeping with tears of grief.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Rāhula, saying:
"Why do you now stand before me, weeping with tears and lamenting?
Rāhula replied, "It is so, World-Honored One.
Previously, I was staying in the Śītavana cemetery at the Pāṅkajāta grove in the city of Rājagṛha."
In that great charnel ground,
there were at that time various celestial spirits (*deva*), dragon spirits (*nāga*), yakṣas, rākṣasas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, garuḍas,
and all other humans and non-humans.
Pretas, bhūtas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others all come to possess me; likewise,
there are many kinds of diverse birds— magpies, crows, foxes, jackals, wolves— and various insects and ants.
"It distresses me greatly.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Rāhula, saying:
"Rāhula, listen attentively now; there is this great, luminous, secret, and difficult-to-grasp dhāraṇī."
For the protection of the listeners,
so that the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās may obtain benefit and happiness for a long night.
He spoke this dhāraṇī, saying: *tadyathā | āgagaga-paga-saṃsara*.

Namaḥ samantabhadra svāhā. (131) Furthermore, Rāhula:
Those who recite this Great Vidyā Dhāraṇī should be able to make offerings of incense and flowers; furthermore,
having bound the mudrās and recited it with a sincere mind one hundred and eight times, they should tie various cords upon their hands and place them around their necks.
One will immediately attain pervasive protection throughout a hundred *yojanas*,
such that humans and non-humans alike will all keep their distance.
Furthermore, one shall not be burned by fire or swept away by water, nor afflicted by blades, staves, poisons, malarial fevers, or malignant diseases.
One cannot be harmed, nor shall one meet an untimely death; the *vitanda* disease and the spells of sorcery shall not prevail.
By reciting this mantra, one attains peace and happiness in all things.
If one is bound by others, one shall immediately obtain liberation from all calamities and afflictions.
It is said that even reciting [this] will completely eliminate quarrels and disputes.
If there are malevolent spirits who come to cause disturbances and do not retreat or disperse,
one need only recite this mantra with single-minded devotion.
When those spirits and deities behold the practitioner who maintains the recitation,
they see him as the Great Yakṣa Lord Vajrapāṇi, composed entirely of vajra,
fierce, majestic, and ablaze with a torrent of flaming fire.
The Four Great Heavenly Kings each brandish iron wheels and sharp swords and blades,
pursuing and dispersing them so that their heads are split into seven pieces and their bodies are torn asunder.
If that ghost-spirit returns to its original dwelling place,
its fellow kindred will not allow it to enter their assembly,
nor will they permit it to dwell in the great royal city of Aṭakāvatī.
Furthermore, Rāhula, if you recite and maintain this Mahāvidyā Dhāraṇī of Durdharṣa with a sincere mind,
you will immediately become free from kings, thieves, water, fire, poisonous vapors, and weapons.
Those who travel through wildernesses, mountain forests,
and perilous evil paths will all be free from fear. Furthermore, Rāhula:
This Mahāvidyā Dhāraṇī of Canda has been spoken,
is being spoken, and will be spoken by ninety-one times the sands of the Ganges Buddhas.
Endowed with supernormal powers,
this one of great supernatural might is surrounded and venerated by all classes of beings— devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
Those sentient beings were freed from all fear and attained peace and happiness.
Then, the Venerable Rāhula and the great assembly, having heard what the World-Honored One had spoken, received it with single-minded faith, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
